entities.summary:
Maffeo Gherardi (1406–1492), elevated to Cardinal-Priest of Santi Marcellino e Pietro by Pope Innocent VIII in 1489, was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic bishop whose career spanned the political and ecclesiastical complexities of the late Quattrocento. As Patriarch of Venice from 1468 until his death, Gherardi occupied a pivotal position within the powerful Venetian Republic, serving as a spiritual leader while navigating the Republic's often contentious relationship with the Holy See. His unexpected elevation to the cardinalate, initially resisted by the Venetian Senate, underscores the intricate balance of power between secular states and the Papacy during an era of burgeoning national identities and papal consolidation.

Gherardi's early career saw him rise through the Augustinian order, eventually becoming General of the Canons Regular of San Salvatore of Bologna. His administrative acumen and theological learning earned him the Patriarchate of Venice, a see of immense prestige and strategic importance. Despite his election as cardinal by Pope Innocent VIII on March 9, 1489, the Venetian Senate initially refused to permit him to accept the honor, fearing it would compromise their sovereignty and grant the Pope too much influence within their territories. It was only after protracted diplomatic negotiations and the personal intervention of Doge Agostino Barbarigo that Gherardi was finally allowed to travel to Rome and receive the red hat, albeit with strict conditions imposed by Venice to safeguard its independence.
